title: cross-cluster burst handshake and reservation negotiator
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Introduce cross-cluster reservation handshake and telemetry; adds backward-compatible controller and API surface for multi-cluster burst reservations. Requires coordinated config rollouts for dedicated fleets to enable negotiation. No breaking changes for existing configs.
description: Motivation: Operators running Dedicated across multiple clusters requested stronger burst guarantees that can be coordinated across cluster boundaries without hard-reserving capacity in a single cluster. Existing warm-pool and burst token approaches work well intra-cluster but leak headroom when traffic spikes hop between regions. What this PR does (single-string description): Adds a cross-cluster reservation "handshake" layer (reservation negotiator) that lets two or more Dedicated clusters negotiate temporary burst credits and soft guarantees. The negotiator is an opt-in controller that runs on the control plane and implements a simple leaseback-style protocol: offer -> accept -> provision -> reconcile -> release. The implementation is conservative by default: if the remote cluster cannot honor a request within the configured window, the local cluster gracefully falls back to local soft-burst without causing hard evictions. Key components: 1) controller/fleet/negotiator.go — core state machine and gRPC-handshake; 2) apis/v1alpha/fleet_reservation.proto — negotiation messages and counters (versioned); 3) pkg/observability/cross_cluster_metrics.go — new telemetry: cross_cluster_offer_count, cross_cluster_accept_rate, cross_cluster_lease_latency_ms, cross_cluster_fallback_ratio; 4) controller changes to admission flow to consult negotiator when local headroom below threshold; 5) integration tests and e2e harness changes to simulate delayed accept and preemption scenarios. Design notes and safety: the handshake is built to avoid hard guarantees across administrative domains. Negotiated reservations are soft and time-bounded (default 30s to 5m depending on pool class). The reconciler continuously monitors utilization deltas with sliding-window smoothing to decide renewals. We deliberately expose a conservative default config (disabled) and feature-flagged rollout (fleet.crossClusterNegotiator.enabled). Migration and rollout strategy: - Phase 1 (safe): controller can be deployed read-only — emits metrics and does dry-run offers to observe cross-cluster acceptance rates. - Phase 2 (opt-in): enable negotiation for specific fleets via the new FleetReservationPolicy CRD field `crossClusterEnable:true` and a per-fleet maxBorrowPct (default 5%). - Phase 3 (gradual): increase per-fleet budgets and tune window durations based on telemetry. Testing and CI: Unit tests for state transitions and failure modes included. New deterministic integration test simulates 3 clusters with synthetic latency to validate fallback and recovery loops. Load tests run in perf-lab to ensure no regressions in admission latency. Security and ops: Negotiation messages are signed with the same mTLS identity used by control-plane components. No extra customer data leaves the clusters — only aggregate counters and reservation tokens are exchanged. Audit entries added for offer/accept/reject flows. Related work and references: - Linear ENG-2489 (cross-cluster reservations spec) - SUP-9821 (support request: cross-region burst failures) High-level summary: This change reduces observed cross-region tail failures during bursty traffic patterns by allowing short-lived, negotiated borrowing of spare headroom from nearby clusters while preserving graceful local fallback behavior. It ships behind a feature flag and includes telemetry to guide safe rollout.
